verdict.rationale: LangGraph's own docs say agent workflows are modeled as graphs of State, Nodes and Edges, that agents and other patterns can be embedded as nodes, and that composing nodes and edges creates looping workflows. Parallelism is corroborated only by community reports ("Pregel/BSP-based orchestration for cycles and parallelism", "built-in parallelism"), and branching is never explicitly documented in the evidence. missing for 10: first-party documentation of conditional branching/routing edges, first-party documentation of parallel (fan-out/fan-in) step execution.

support.subject: As a developer, I can compose agents into an explicit graph or workflow with branching, loops, and parallel steps

citations.quote: LangGraph models agent workflows as graphs. You define the behavior of your agents using three key components: State, Nodes, Edges.
By composing Nodes and Edges, you can create complex, looping workflows that evolve the state over time.
Embed other patterns as nodes in your workflow.
It's a Pregel/BSP-based orchestration for cycles and parallelism without data races; can design your graph as a state machine.
built-in parallelism in LangGraph, while promising, can complicate debugging a lot
